changes: Corsicana is explained: 910 MW take-or-pay 'regardless of utilization', rent within 60 days of pad delivery, tenant owns modules and pays opex, about 33% unlevered yield on about $5.5bn.

Funding plan disclosed: base case 80% to 90% loan-to-cost, $4.4bn to $4.9bn non-recourse from 2027; fallback, tenant funds reimbursements with rent credits at 12%. Corsicana and Rockdale capital $7.6bn to $7.8bn (portfolio $7.7bn to $7.9bn), debt $6.1bn to $7.0bn, Riot equity $800mn to $1.5bn through mid-2028.
Riot's sources: about $2.1bn, being $950mn liquidity, about $900mn rent before debt service, $180mn expected AMD term loan and $110mn other. Only the $950mn is in hand. No project debt has closed.
Same 1 GW load supports 910 MW against 756 MW on a Tier 3 design, and capital about halves, with $130/kW-month starting rent.
Mining at Corsicana winds down around summer 2027; lease revenue guided at about $23mn in 2026, $250mn in 2027, $1.8bn in 2028 and $2.3bn in 2029.

consensus_thesis: Investors own Riot as a power-rich Texas landlord with 241 MW leased, a non-binding Corsicana LOI, and funding from bitcoin sales and project debt instead of new shares, and they doubt the backstop, the bridge refinancing and the value of unleased power.
headline: The consensus view should move up: the call shows a credible way to fund Corsicana, and project-level returns are high, but credit quality improves only if the 2027 debt closes, since one lab without an investment-grade rating holds about 96% of contracted MW and the $573mn bridge's 31 December maturity went unaddressed.
kona: Corsicana is the closest listed comparison for a model Kona has not priced: powered land, where the tenant owns the modules, at about $6mn per MW and $130/kW-month starting rent, about $178/MWh of IT load before energy on our arithmetic. Kona should price it as a fifth option, copy take-or-pay on all MW regardless of utilization and rent starting within 60 days of delivery, and copy the 12% tenant-funded fallback. Caution: Riot got this with 1 GW of approved power and an entire campus; at tens of MW Kona has less leverage, and the tenant is one lab.

sections.body: Dilution and per-share: no equity in 2026 per release; 375.1mn shares. The $594.4mn 0.75% converts (about 40mn shares, $14.86 conversion) are close to the money. Book debt $656.6mn, with only $67.5mn current, and the bridge had $20.8mn principal drawn at 30 September ($12.8mn net), non-recourse, to be repaid from long-term project financing (10-Q). Rate check: 10-Q base rent is $130/kW-month with 3% escalators, which averages about $161 over 15 years and about $26.4bn on a simple start; the stated $28bn implies about $171. The 10-Q runs the term 15 years from Phase 3, so earlier phases pay longer, which explains about $1.2bn on our arithmetic, leaving about $0.4bn; management did not address it. Year-one run-rate on 400 MW is about $624mn. Price: $15.37 close on 4 November (+9.6%), $14.43 at 9:47 ET on 5 November (-6.1%). No bond quote found; market cap about $5.4bn on 375.1mn shares.
